messages:
sara-sales: Quick sync — large banking customer wants a capacity commit. They expect 1.8k RPS typical with short bursts up to ~5k for ~30s. Asking: how many reserved GPUs should we propose, what autoscale policy, and cost/fallback options? Also KMS requirement in security questionnaire. Any red flags?

alex-se: First pass: size for a steady baseline and then support burst via a separate pool. For short prompts we can likely keep a moderate reserved baseline and autoscale into a burst pool. Need exact request token profile to pick numbers. :mag: 

pradeep-ml: Do we have model throughput figures? For gptx-large quantized to 4-bit we benchmark ~450 tokens/s per GPU at seq=2048. But requests are short so tokens/request matters a lot.

alex-se: Quick calc example (rough):
```
If avg output 40 tokens + input 20 = 60 tokens
Req/s per GPU = 450 / 60 = 7.5 req/s
To support 1,200 RPS -> GPUs_needed = 1,200 / 7.5 = 160 GPUs
```
That shows how sensitive this is to tokens/request. We need the real profile.

sara-sales: Updated from customer: most requests are tiny — avg 6 input tokens, 8 output tokens, and ~70% classification/chat light, 30% embeddings. So ~14 tokens per request on average.

pradeep-ml: Recalc with 14 tokens/request:
```
Req/s per GPU = 450 / 14 ≈ 32 req/s
Baseline 1,200 RPS -> ~38 GPUs
Burst 5,000 RPS -> ~157 GPUs
```
So a reasonable commercial proposal: reserved baseline ~38–45 GPUs regionally (spread across 2 AZs), plus a burst pool for peak (~120–160 GPUs) with autoscale.

jordan-ops: Ops caveat: spinning 100+ GPUs for short spikes is costly and has provisioning latency. Recommend a warm standby pool (nodes already up with model loaded) plus an autoscale group of preemptible nodes. Autoscale trigger should be queue depth + request latency thresholds, and scale-down cooldown should be ~30–60s to avoid thrash.

rachel-security: KMS note: customer wants their CMK. We can support customer-managed keys in Private deployments easily. Hosted requires additional cross-account KMS setup and legal sign-off. I’ll start the security questionnaire entries and flag any blockers.

alex-se: Proposed autoscale policy for the deck:
- Baseline: reserved pool = 40 GPUs split 2 AZs
- Warm pool: 8–12 ready nodes per AZ with model loaded
- Burst group: autoscale up to 160 GPUs (on-demand + spot mix) when queue_depth > 150 for >10s or p95 latency > 300ms
- Fallback: automatic routing to a smaller quantized model (gptx-compact-4q) when burst capacity unavailable; degrade gracefully with SLA note.

sara-sales: Customer requirement: p95 latency must stay < 350ms, otherwise they won't sign. Can we realistically guarantee that with the above?

pradeep-ml: p95 depends on queuing. With regional AZ split + warm pool the risk is lower. Need to run a trace-driven simulation to estimate p95. I'll take the customer's trace once they share.

jordan-ops: I'll draft the autoscale + warm-pool runbook: queue-depth -> scale-up steps, AZ affinity, cooldowns, and controller alerts. Also add a manual failover to lower-fidelity model for cost/latency protection.

reserve-bot: reserved-pool created (stub) — baseline 40 GPUs requested across az-a/az-b for test.

alex-se: Action items: 1) customer to share real request trace (sara). 2) pradeep + alex run perf sim against trace and produce GPU counts + p95 estimate. 3) jordan draft autoscale/warm-pool runbook and cost implications. 4) rachel complete KMS + security questionnaire answers. 5) sales to present tiered pricing: reserved baseline + burst credits + degraded-model fallback pricing.

sara-sales: Thanks — I'll ask for the trace and update. Marking this for follow-up once perf sim and runbook are in. :white_check_mark:
